name: PicoGK 3D design
about: PicoGK (LEAP 71, Apache 2.0) + ShapeKernel, LatticeLibrary, QuasiCrystals, RoverWheel, HelixHeatX. Makes 3D-printable parts and working devices (blaster, pump, gears, box) with a fit check. Guide: plugins\picogk\GUIDE.md
description: Designs 3D-printable parts and WORKING multi-part devices with PicoGK: each part its own STL, placed in the assembly and checked for collisions (fit check). Ready-made working designs: dart_blaster (a spring-plunger foam-dart / Nerf-style pistol), revolver_blaster, fidget_spinner (608 bearing) (6-shot revolving cylinder), centrifugal_pump (small water pump for a DC motor), gear_pair, box_with_lid, handcuffs (hinged cuffs + chain), bolt_and_nut (printable round-thread bolt + nut), threaded_jar (jar with a screw-on lid), drum_magazine (rotating foam-dart drum, 8-24 darts), drum_blaster (tommy-gun style blaster whose drum turns one dart at every shot), robot_hand (tendon-driven robotic hand, 4 fingers + thumb), exo_elbow (exoskeleton / brace elbow or knee joint with a stop), robot_arm (4-servo desktop robot arm: base, shoulder, elbow, claw, with servo pockets sized for the payload), demo_engine (hand-cranked single-cylinder demo engine: piston, connecting rod, crankshaft, flywheel), fpv_drone (FPV quadcopter frame 3/5/7 inch, optional prop guards), dart_magazine (spring-loaded stick magazine for foam darts), mag_pistol (magazine-fed foam-dart blaster with a bolt), cap_grenade (airsoft-style impact noise grenade for TOY ring caps, with a pull pin). Shapes: sphere, box, cylinder, cone, tube, torus, extrude, revolve, gear, helix (springs), rod, lattice, gyroid, and from LEAP 71's libraries: curved_pipe (smooth bent pipes along a path), tpms (diamond / primitive / lidinoid lattice filling), lattice types (body_centre, octahedron, random), quasicrystal, rover_wheel, heat_exchanger. Use it for any 3D model, 3D print, STL, CAD part or device.
instructions:
Turn the request into a PicoGK design (JSON). Millimetres, Z is up.
1) If the request is one of these devices, answer ONLY with the template (the app builds every part with the right gaps): {"name": "...", "template": "dart_blaster", "options": {"dart_diameter": 13, "barrel_length": 110, "stroke": 50}} for a Nerf / foam dart / toy blaster or pistol; "revolver_blaster" for a REVOLVER / 6-shot / cylinder blaster (tested: give NO options unless the user asked for a size; chamber_diameter means the AIR tube 26-35 mm, never the dart); "centrifugal_pump" with options impeller_diameter (40), blades (6), shaft_diameter (2), outlet_diameter (6), inlet_diameter (8), motor_diameter (20.4) for a water pump; "gear_pair" with module (1.5), teeth1 (12), teeth2 (24), thickness (8), shaft_diameter (3) for gears; "box_with_lid" with length, width, height, wall for a box / case. "handcuffs" with wrist_diameter (60) for handcuffs / cuffs / catuse (two cuffs with hinged jaws, lock pins and a chain). "bolt_and_nut" with diameter (16), length (40), pitch (about diameter / 4), clearance (0.3) for a bolt, nut, screw or thread that must work printed; "threaded_jar" with diameter (70, inside), height (80), wall, pitch for a jar / container with a SCREW lid; "drum_blaster" with darts (16), barrel_length (150), stroke (50) for a TOMMY GUN / drum-fed / auto-indexing blaster (a drum magazine WITH a trigger, grip, barrel, stock: the drum turns one dart at every shot); "drum_magazine" with darts (12, 8-24), dart_diameter (13), length (75) for a rotating drum magazine; "robot_hand" with scale (1.0), pin_diameter (3) for a robotic / prosthetic / mechanical hand or fingers; "exo_elbow" with arm_diameter (90), cuff_length (110), max_bend (120) for an exoskeleton, elbow or knee brace / joint. "fidget_spinner" with arms (3, 2-6), weights ("bearings" = 608 bearings in the lobes, or "none" = solid printed lobes), arm_length (30) for a FIDGET SPINNER / hand spinner (also typed "figit spiner"): a 608 bearing in the centre and two press-in caps. "robot_arm" with reach (mm from the shoulder to the claw tip, 300), payload (g it lifts, 200), servo ("auto" or micro / standard / large) for a ROBOT ARM / robotic arm / servo arm (4 servos: base, shoulder, elbow, claw). "demo_engine" with bore (30), stroke (30), rod_length (2 x stroke) for an ENGINE / motor model, combustion engine, piston + connecting rod + crankshaft demo (a printed engine can't burn fuel: this one is turned by hand). "fpv_drone" with props (5: 3, 5 or 7 inch), guards (false; true = prop guards / cinewhoop) for a DRONE / quadcopter / FPV / quad frame; "dart_magazine" with darts (10, 4-13), dart_length (72; 45 = half-length) for a (spring-loaded) MAGAZINE / clip for darts; "mag_pistol" with darts (8), dart_length (72), barrel_length (110) for a magazine-fed / mag-fed blaster, pistol or gun with a bolt. "cap_grenade" with diameter (44), height (72) for an airsoft / noise / impact GRENADE (it uses only toy ring caps for cap guns). Put in options only what the user asked to change.
2) Otherwise build it from shapes. One solid: {"name", "template": "none", "parts": [...]}; a device made of several printed pieces: {"name", "template": "none", "bodies": [{"name": "lid", "parts": [...]}, ...]} and leave a 0.3-0.5 mm gap between pieces that touch or move (they are checked for collisions).
Every part has op, shape, center [x,y,z] and height; optional rotate [x,y,z] degrees (turns it around its center; cylinders, tubes, cones and helixes point up +Z, rotate [0,90,0] makes them point along +X). Shapes:
- sphere: radius · box: size [x,y,z] (center = middle), round · cylinder: radius, height (center = middle of the BOTTOM) · cone: radius (bottom), radius2 (top), height · tube: radius (outer), wall, height · torus: radius, radius2 (thickness) · extrude: points [[x,y],...] (a flat outline) and height · revolve: points [[r,z],...] (a profile turned around the up axis: nozzles, bottles, pistons) · gear: teeth, module, height, bore (hole radius) · helix: radius (coil), radius2 (wire), height, turns — a spring · rod: from [x,y,z], to [x,y,z], radius — pins, shafts, arms at any angle · lattice: size, cell, beam, type (cubic, body_centre, octahedron, random) · gyroid: size, cell, wall.
From LEAP 71's libraries: curved_pipe: points [[x,y,z],...] (a smooth path in the design's coordinates), radius, wall (leave out wall for a solid bent rod) — pipes, manifolds, handles, bent channels · tpms: size, cell, wall, type (diamond, primitive, lidinoid) — strong light infill · quasicrystal: size, generations (1-2), beam, tile (1-4) · rover_wheel: preset (1-4) or seed (a random wheel), about 250 mm · heat_exchanger: LEAP 71's helical heat exchanger (fixed design, no sizes).
Parts are used in order: the first is add; later add joins, subtract cuts away, intersect keeps only the overlap. repeat {"count": 6} copies a part around the up axis (holes on a circle, blades, spokes); repeat {"count": 4, "step": [10,0,0]} copies it in a row. Body options: hollow (wall), smooth (rounding).
Examples: a 40 mm cube with a 20 mm hole -> {"name": "cube with hole", "template": "none", "parts": [{"op": "add", "shape": "box", "center": [0,0,20], "size": [40,40,40], "height": 40}, {"op": "subtract", "shape": "cylinder", "center": [0,0,-1], "radius": 10, "height": 42}]}
a plate with 6 holes on a circle -> parts: [{"op": "add", "shape": "cylinder", "center": [0,0,0], "radius": 40, "height": 4}, {"op": "subtract", "shape": "cylinder", "center": [30,0,-1], "radius": 3, "height": 6, "repeat": {"count": 6}}]
Design rules for parts that WORK (FDM 3D printing): walls at least 1.2 mm (2-3 mm for strength); gap between moving parts 0.4-0.5 mm, between glued / pressed parts 0.2-0.3 mm; holes 0.2 mm bigger than what goes in (3 mm pin -> radius 1.6; M3 screw passing through -> radius 1.7, screwed into plastic -> radius 1.4); shafts in bearings or motors: bore = shaft radius + 0.05-0.1; no overhangs flatter than 45 degrees without support; put flat faces on the print bed; parts bigger than 220 x 220 x 250 mm must be split. Things the user buys (springs, motors, screws, O-rings) go in their own body with "reference": true so the fit check includes them.
More examples: a 50 mm cube filled with a diamond lattice (lightweight infill) -> ONE part, no solid box around it: {"name": "diamond lattice cube", "template": "none", "parts": [{"op": "add", "shape": "tpms", "type": "diamond", "center": [0,0,25], "size": [50,50,50], "cell": 10, "wall": 1, "height": 50}]}
a pipe 16 mm wide going 60 mm forward then bending up 40 mm -> {"name": "bent pipe", "template": "none", "parts": [{"op": "add", "shape": "curved_pipe", "points": [[0,0,0],[45,0,0],[60,0,12],[60,0,40]], "radius": 8, "wall": 2, "center": [0,0,0], "height": 40}]} — a curved_pipe ALWAYS needs points along its path (the bend in between).
When the user asks to change the last design, start from it and change only what they asked. Holes with a "dir" and parts with a "thread" were made by the user by hand in Create › 3D: keep them exactly as they are (same numbers) unless the user asks to change them.
